headline: Argentina thrash Burkina Faso 7-0 in dominant friendly display
summary: Argentina continued their impressive form with a resounding 7-0 victory over Burkina Faso in a friendly. This marks their second consecutive win, scoring 11 goals without conceding.
details: Argentina produced another dominant attacking display on Sunday, thrashing Burkina Faso 7-0 at the Monumental Stadium in their second friendly match of the FIFA international break. This victory followed an impressive 4-0 win over Bolivia, giving Lionel Scaloni's side back-to-back victories and 11 goals across the two matches without conceding.
Argentina wasted no time, taking the lead just four minutes in. Lautaro Martínez scored from a rebound after his initial penalty was saved, marking his second consecutive goal for the national team.

The hosts quickly doubled their advantage in the eighth minute with an own goal from Moumouni Diallo. Gianluca Prestianni added a third in the 12th minute, scoring his first goal for Argentina and putting them three goals ahead within the first quarter of an hour.
Nicolás Paz extended the lead to 4-0 in the 35th minute, followed by Julián Álvarez making it 5-0 just one minute later. Argentina went into halftime with a commanding five-goal advantage.
The dominance continued after the interval, with substitute Franco Mastantuono scoring his first national team goal in the 57th minute. He calmly converted a one-on-one opportunity to make it 6-0.

Burkina Faso struggled throughout the match, unable to contain Argentina's relentless attack. The seventh and final goal came deep into stoppage time, with Giovanni Simeone completing the emphatic 7-0 victory in the 93rd minute.

topic: Govt employees arrears with October salary
headline_marked: [[Government employees to get 3 months' arrears]] with October salary, calculation starts tomorrow
headline: Government employees to get 3 months' arrears with October salary, calculation starts tomorrow
summary: The new pay structure will see varying arrears based on individual pay fixation, a process that begins tomorrow and must conclude by October 20.
details: Government officials and employees are set to receive approximately three months of salary arrears along with their October pay. The exact amount each individual receives will depend on the new pay fixation process, which is scheduled to begin tomorrow, Monday, and must be completed by October 20.

This pay fixation will be conducted through the iBAS++ module, where employees must submit personal and service-related information including NID, date of birth, current position, grade, joining date, and basic salary. Previous pay fixation details also need verification.

The new basic salary will be determined via this process, and arrears will be calculated based on the difference between old and new salaries, factoring in the effective date. The government will disburse these three months of arrears in a lump sum, though amounts will vary based on grade and individual pay structure.

The new national pay scale, implemented via a September 19 gazette after 11 years, sets minimum basic pay at BDT 20,000 and maximum at BDT 156,000. Full salary and allowances will be phased in over the 2026-27 and 2027-28 fiscal years.

Specifically, 40% of the difference between new and old basic salaries will be paid from July 1 to December 31 this year, increasing to 70% from January 1 to June 30, 2027. The full new basic salary becomes effective from July 1, 2027, with allowances from January 1, 2028.

Employees with promotions, transfers, time scales, or higher grades must provide supporting documents. Accurate submission of all details, including name, NID, and salary history, is crucial, as discrepancies may require corrections and delay the process.

Finance Division officials are addressing complexities for employees who received time scales, selection grades, or higher grades under the old structure. New rules specify that those with two or more such benefits in the same position previously are not eligible for further higher grades, while those with one may qualify for a second after six more years.
